process_global_statics.description: `static` items (including `static mut`) under crates/*/src whose DECLARED TYPE contains one of Mutex, RwLock, Atomic, OnceLock, OnceCell, LazyLock, 'Lazy<', 'Cell<', RefCell - or that REACHES one of them through a `type` alias or a named struct declared in the SAME file, so a global cannot duck the metric by being given a name. A static inside a `thread_local! { ... }` block is EXCLUDED (per-thread by definition). Test-gated (#[cfg(test)]) statics COUNT: under `cargo test --lib` sibling tests share one process, so a test-only global is exactly the seam that flakes. Non-test file = the same definition as giant_files (no 'tests/' or 'tests_*/' directory component, filename not tests.rs / *_tests.rs / tests_*.rs); vendor/ and target/ excluded. Recomputed by scripts/ratchet/process_globals.py; `--list` prints every hit as `path:line NAME: type`, with ` [via NAME]` naming the local alias or struct a resolved hit went through.

_attribution.summary: 38 -> 33 on 2026-09-11 (PR-2 of the per-vault ownership migration). Eight statics are gone and the scanner's alias gap is closed, which adds three that were always real. Every one of the 33 below is named with its bucket and its reason; there is no residue class left to work through.
_attribution.law: Engine state belongs to a vault (a field on StoreCore, the Arc-shared inner handle every Store and Vault reaches) or to a thread (thread_local!, when writer and reader are the same thread by construction). The process owns only locks that mirror an OS or LMDB rule, write-once registries and plugin doors, and monotonic id allocators. Every remaining static below is named with its bucket reason; a new one is a stated decision in its PR (AGENTS.md ratchet law).
_attribution.why_it_exists: Two flakes in one week came from process-global mutable state that tests read or arm. #922: the BM25 diagnostics counters are process-wide, so a sibling test in the same `cargo test --lib` binary moved them under a test that asserted on them. #923: the delete rendezvous slot is a single process-global Mutex, so two raced-delete tests clobbered each other's channel; the fix made that seam thread-local. PR-1 (#927) and PR-2 (#929) of the per-vault ownership migration moved or deleted every engine counter and test seam a vault could own; this counter now stops the class regrowing.

pr2_2026_09_11.locks_moved_onto_the_vault_2: batch/export/foreign_stage/export_foreign_stage.rs STAGED_IMPORT_ADMISSION_LOCK and sync/client/federated.rs STAGED_IMPORT_LOCK -> StoreCore.staged_import_admission_lock and .staged_import_confirm_lock, both production fields under #[cfg(feature = "sync")]. The design left these undecided pending evidence. Every row inside either critical section is addressed through the vault that owns it - the receipt row, the staged content row and the selector admission all go through `vault.store.sync_state` - so neither guards a shared host path, and a process-wide lock was serializing unrelated vaults for nothing.

It never counted toward this metric (it lives under a tests/ path), but it is the cost the shared seam was imposing - seven raced-delete tests that had to run one at a time.
pr2_2026_09_11.scanner_alias_gap_closed: The metric read the DECLARED type, so an alias or a named struct hid a global from it. process_globals.py now resolves both when they are declared in the same file, and the three surviving known_gap_4_statics items are counted: store/test_hooks.rs BEFORE_LMDB_OPEN and AFTER_LMDB_OPEN (LmdbOpenHookSlot) and oneiron-remote/src/embedded.rs REGISTRY (a Registry struct holding an AtomicU32 and a LazyLock<Mutex<HashMap>>). The fourth, STAGED_IMPORT_PRE_CONTENT_HOOK, this PR deleted. Resolution is same-file and textual; a cross-file alias would still hide one, which is stated rather than guessed at.

raw_hasher_starts.description: Matches of `blake3::(hash|derive_key|keyed_hash)(`, `blake3::Hasher::new` and `Sha256::(new|digest)(` in .rs files under crates/*/src (same non-test definition as giant_files), outside the paths scripts/ratchet/raw_hasher_allowlist.txt lists, each with its reason (scope `all`, or `sha256` for a file where an outside party fixes SHA-256). Recomputed by scripts/ratchet/raw_hasher_starts.py (no cargo); `--list` prints every hit. It blocks no merge: the merge pipeline counts each change merged into main and reports a raise to its author, who lowers the count in a follow-up PR (lead 2026-11-16, RATCHET-GATE-MERGE-BAR = A).

_attribution.summary: Added by PLAN-UC-04 stage 0 (fable pass 22, one fingerprint primitive), measured at main eed5070979c3: 2400 starts with an empty allowlist, 2355 after the allowlist (45 starts: the class A and B SHA-256 files of DESIGN section 2.4, oneiron-crypto, the two oneiron-seal files an RFC fixes, and gate/resolution/frontier_hash.rs with frontier_hash/, which Setting 6d deletes). A file that mixes an outside-fixed digest with an engine digest is counted, not allowlisted; stage 7 moves the outside-fixed one into its own allowlisted module. The new crate's own 6 starts are allowlisted. The design pass measured 2399 at 570f051b78da with the same pattern and file rule. Re-measured at main aee268f795d1 (2026-11-15 20:5x): 2356; the +1 is crates/oneiron-llm/src/oneiron_rpc/mesh/mod.rs:217 (`blake3::hash`), from the oneiron-llm family fold 35a1c00f36c.
_attribution.law: A new hash goes through oneiron_contracts::fingerprint (a v1 purpose from the registry in crates/oneiron-fingerprint/src/purposes/) or ContentHash. A digest that main already stores or sends keeps its bytes through a legacy purpose (the K door) until the launch reset (stage 9).
_attribution.expected_direction: Down only. Each PLAN-UC-04 stage 1-7 PR lowers this count to its new value and says why in bump_reason; the long tail is done when it is 0. A path joins the allowlist only in a reviewed PR, with its reason on the same line.

hand_name_tables.description: Lists of names spelled by hand in .rs files under crates/*/src (same non-test definition as giant_files), outside the paths scripts/ratchet/hand_name_tables_allowlist.txt lists, each with its reason: a fn returning `&str` with two or more arms `Type::Variant => "name"` (forward), a fn with two or more arms `"name" => Type::Variant`, bare or in `Some(` or `Ok(` (reverse), and a `const` array or slice of two or more `Type::Variant` (list). Every string in a table is name-shaped (1 to 64 bytes of letters, digits and `_ . : / -`), every variant a unit path, comments and the insides of literals are blanked first, and a type that derives `Register` in the same file is skipped (its other string methods are fact columns). Recomputed by scripts/ratchet/hand_name_tables.py (no cargo); `--list` prints every table and `--names` every forward row. The script also exits 1 when two `#[register("...")]` lines give one name.

_attribution.summary: Added by Fable pass 25 (the Register pattern, step R1), measured on main 55e034509eb1 (after PLAN-UC-04 stage 0, #8155) on 2026-11-15: 1371 with an empty allowlist, 1255 after it (the crates with no dependency on oneiron-contracts, which cannot name the trait, and oneiron-derive, the proc-macro crate that writes the derive). The design pass measured 1361 and 1248 at e1f11f55cfef with its trial detector, which also skipped every file holding neither `enum` nor `=>`.
_attribution.law: A new list of names is declared once as a Register: a plain enum with `#[derive(Register)]` and `#[register("lower.dotted")]` (oneiron_contracts::register), whose names come from the enum's own serde attributes. A hand table is converted when its file is next touched, with a names test generated from `--names` that proves no stored or sent name changed (M-1 keep).
_attribution.expected_direction: Down only. Adopting PRs do not edit this count; the Engine lowers it once per train. The count blocks no merge (lead 2026-11-16, REG-1 = B): the merge pipeline reports a raise to the change's author, who lowers it in a follow-up PR. A path joins the allowlist only in a reviewed PR, with its reason on the same line.

test_lint_sleep.description: Sleep calls in Rust test code under crates/ and apps/: `sleep(`, `sleep_until(` and `sleep_ms(` called as a function (not a method, not a definition), in code only (comments and string literals are blanked first). Test code is every file under a `tests` or `tests_*` directory, every tests.rs, *_tests.rs, *_test.rs and tests_*.rs, every file with an inner `#![cfg(test)]`, and the item after each `#[cfg(test)]`-style attribute in any other file; directories named target, vendor, node_modules, .git and fixtures-out and the vendored crates/heed, crates/paste and crates/loro are skipped. A line opts out with `testkit-lint: allow(sleep) <reason>` on it, or on a comment line just above it; an allow with no reason allows nothing. Recomputed by scripts/ratchet/test_lint.py (no cargo; `--list --rule sleep` prints each finding, `--baseline` the per-file counts in the Rust lint's baseline form). Wait on a barrier, a channel or the fake clock instead.
